title.narrative: Central Sulawesi Rehabilitation and Reconstruction Project

description.narrative: The PDO is to reconstruct and strengthen public facilities and safer housing in selected disaster-affected areas.

The disasters that Indonesia experienced in 2018 caused the highest losses of lives in over a decade. In July and August 2018, West Nusa Tenggara (NTB) province suffered a series of major earthquakes, the most significant occurring on 5 August 2018 measuring M7.0, which affected the entire island's population of around 3.5 million as well as thousands of tourists. The National Disaster Management Authority (BNPB) confirmed that the earthquakes caused 561 fatalities and displaced over 396,000 people , damaging almost 110,000 houses, 663 schools, 52 health facilities, 6 bridges, and many roads, causing approximately USD854 million in damages and losses. In September 2018, a M7.5 earthquake with an epicenter located 81 kilometers north of Palu City in Central Sulawesi caused strong ground shaking and near field tsunamis that damaged coastal settlements along Palu Bay. This disaster caused an estimated 2,227 fatalities (with many more missing); USD1.3 billion in economic losses, estimated at 13.7 percent of regional GDP ; and displaced almost 165,000 people . In December 2018, the eruption and subsequent partial collapse of Anak Krakatau Volcano led to a tsunami that affected coastal settlements in Banten and Lampung provinces along Sunda Strait, causing 437 fatalities, displacing almost 34,000 people, and damaging tourism infrastructure including 92 hotels and 60 culinary stalls. The PDO would be achieved through three key components: (1) Resilient construction of permanent housing units and settlement infrastructure (2) Resilient reconstruction and strengthening of public facilities;; and (3) Project Implementation Support (including capacity building and contingencies).

title.narrative: Constructed houses built in resettlement sites provided with direct access to a paved road network

comment.narrative: The project exceeded its target by providing direct access to paved roads to 107.78% of the 3,600 targeted houses, surpassing the 90% target threshold. In practice, providing direct access to paved roads was provided to all 3,880 houses constructed under CSRRP. However, when compared to the original target of 7,000 houses before restructuring, this represents a more modest achievement of 55.4% of the initially planned coverage.

title.narrative: Reconstructed houses provided with sanitation system

comment.narrative: The project exceeded its target by providing sanitation system to 107.78% of the 3,600 targeted houses, surpassing the 90% target threshold. In practice, sanitation system was extended to all 3,880 houses constructed under CSRRP. However, when compared to the original target of 7,000 houses before restructuring, this represents a more modest achievement of 55.4% of the initially planned coverage.

title.narrative: Reconstructed houses provided with housing connection for water supply

comment.narrative: The project exceeded its target by providing water supply connections to 107.78% of the 3,600 targeted houses, surpassing the 90% target threshold. In practice, water supply access was extended to all 3,880 houses constructed under CSRRP. However, when compared to the original target of 7,000 houses before restructuring, this represents a more modest achievement of 55.4% of the initially planned coverage.

title.narrative: Education facilities rehabilitated or reconstructed to project's resilience standards

comment.narrative: The project achieved its revised target by completing the rehabilitation and reconstruction of 18 educational facilitiest. Notably, this included a university complex, which is counted as a single facility despite comprising 44 rehabilitated and reconstructed buildings. However, when compared to the original target of 200 educational facilities set at appraisal, this represents a modest achievement of 9% of the initially planned facilities.

title.narrative: Housing units constructed to project's resilience standards

comment.narrative:
The project exceeded its revised target by delivering 3,880 safer, completed housing units.
At appraisal, the project aimed to construct 7,000 housing units. However, further validation refined the eligible DAPs, prompting a target adjustment to 3,600 housing units. When measured against the original target of 7,000 units, the project achieved approximately 55.43% of the planned housing output.

title.narrative: Women that are aware of employment opportunities related to recovery activities in targeted project areas

comment.narrative: The achievement of this indicator is obtained from OSP data on the participation of women (non-DAPs) in dissemination and socialization of job opportunities that encourage women to apply for vacancies as consultants, facilitators, and building supervisors. The participation of non-WTB women in these activities accounts for approximately 3,220 (35%) of the total participants (9115 people).

title.narrative: Women's participation in decision-making process meetings

comment.narrative: This indicator targets women's participation in various meetings, awareness activities, and discussions on decision-making within the project, including the formation of community groups (Pokmas), selection of blocks and plots, environmental management (as volunteers initiating the formation of management organizations/OP), housing development, and livelihood programs. Survey from the OSP team indicates that women's participation in these processes has reached 40%, (10,770 out of 26,845 participants) of the target.

title.narrative: Health facilities rehabilitated or reconstructed to project's resilience standards

comment.narrative: The project has achieved the target under the indicator, by completing reconstruction and rehabilitation of seven health facilities have been completed (Torabelo Hospital, Tipo Health Community Center, Anutapura 2A & 2B Hospital, Undata 2A & 2B Hospital, and three community health centers). The SPLF or building certificates to ensure the compliance of resilience standards for seven packages has been issued.

title.narrative: Women that are aware of land or property title rights in targeted project areas

comment.narrative: The achievement of this indicator is measured through a survey by the OSP targeting female beneficiaries who participated in rights awareness activities, discussions on land legality, and explanations of land status in 19 permanent housing locations. The total female participants is 2,222. The survey results indicate 2015 participants feel that these activities provided benefits, such as women gaining an understanding of land ownership rights, and participants expressing an intention to create joint ownership deeds between husband and wife.

title.narrative: Gender- and disability-inclusive reconstructed public facilities

comment.narrative: The formula to measure this indicator has changed, reducing the value of this indicator. The indicator measures gender and disability-inclusive aspects in completed reconstruction buildings of public facilities. The completed buildings need to comply with a project's checklist of Gender and Universal Access. TMCs and the PMC have had series of reviews during preparation, design, and construction. They have carried out post-construction joint surveys using a Checklist of Gender and Universal Access to measure the indicator. 97% of completed public buildings has been surveyed.

title.narrative: Resilient and inclusive building standards are established for the project

comment.narrative: The PMU and PMC has completed compilation of MPWH's standards on resilience and inclusive buildings that are utilized by CSRRP. Link of the standards is: https://sulteng-sitaba.com/pedoman-teknis/modul-qa-standar-bangunan-gedung-yang-inklusif-dan-berketahanan

comment.narrative:
The grievance redress mechanism is available via the following channels:
1. Offline via face-to-face channel: project staff, local governments, community facilitators, consultants, or contractors.
2. Online channel: a. Hotline number: WhatsApp: +62813-1967-9006 b. Project social media: facebook (csrrp.kemenpupr), instragram (csrrp.kemenpupr), twitter (@csrrp2) c. Email: info.pengaduan@csrrp.org d. Website: https://www.sulteng-sitaba.com/kirim-pengaduan
PMC has a statff that dedicated to manage the GRM. Training on GRM to project staff, local governments, consultants, contractors, and community facilitators has been carried out, including GRM on GBV.

title.narrative: MIS and project website established and functioning

comment.narrative: The project website is https://www.sulteng-sitaba.com/. The website contains reports, MIS, GRM, library and publication, project news, and KPI status.

title.narrative: Served people having strengthened public facilities

comment.narrative:
The CSRRP successfully restored access to resilient public services, serving 236,161 people and slightly exceeding the revised target of 236,101.
Initially, the project aimed to rehabilitate over 230 facilities to serve approximately 760,000 people. However, more detailed planning and analysis shifted the focus to fewer but larger and more complex investments, such as university and hospital complexes, to better meet local needs. This revised approach prioritized facilities with broader service coverage, enabling the project to fully achieve its objective despite a reduced facility count.

title.narrative: Targeted people satisfied with completed housing (disaggregated by gender)

comment.narrative:
Under this indicator, the project aimed for a 70% satisfaction rate among disaster-affected residents. At project completion, 90.3% of residents expressed satisfaction with their new homes, significantly surpassing the original target
In a comprehensive survey conducted by the Evaluation and Study Consultant (ESC), a sample of 778 disaster-affected individuals was assessed. The findings indicate that 728 respondents expressed satisfaction with the permanent housing construction and the associated settlement infrastructure—including water, sanitation, and roads—developed by the project.

title.narrative: Targeted people having safer housing completed and occupied

comment.narrative: The CSRRP exceeded its revised target by relocating 11,358 disaster-affected people (DAPs) into safer, completed homes, achieving 96.79% of the revised target. Initially, the project aimed to relocate 90% of ~22,700 DAPs, but further data validation refined the target to 11,743 households. While this represents ~50% of the original target, the project fully delivered against verified target.

To date, CSRRP received 3,692 inquiries, with 3,593 (94,63%) inquiries/complaints were solved. The inquiries are related to requests for information/data (1,721 inquiries or 48%), problems/complaints/incidents (956 inquiries or 27%), and suggestions/criticism of the project (916 inquiries or 25%).
Update: Upon completion, the project successfully addressed 3,400 out of the 3,593 complaints received. These inquiries comprised requests for information or data (1,721 inquiries, 48%), issues related to problems, complaints, or incidents (956 inquiries, 27%), and suggestions or criticisms of the project (916 inquiries, 25%).

title.narrative: Non-CSRRP housing provided with strengthened settlement infrastructure

comment.narrative: The construction of settlement infrastructure is completed to serve 3.824 housing units in non-CSRRP housing areas. The settlement infrastructure consists of roads, drainages, retaining walls, sanitation, water supply systems, public open spaces, and equipment for solid waste facilities. The non-CSRRP housing areas were built by NSUP-CERC, BNPB/national government, local governments, and NGOs. The settlement infrastructures were built by CSRRP in non-CSRRP housing areas to support GOI, ensuring the reconstructed housing has adequate basic services and the well-functioning of settlement infrastructures in post-disaster areas in Central Sulawesi.

title.narrative: Number of kelurahan/village served with local scale infrastructure

comment.narrative: The Community Grants of community-scale settlement infrastructure financed tertiary infrastructure in 27 kelurahan/villages. The disbursement and construction have completed in 2024. The second tranche of the Grant that was disbursed in 2024 is still under construction. Tertiary infrastructure includes drainage, road, sanitation, retaining wall, water supply system, paved roads, public toilet facilities, and open public spaces.

title.narrative: Other public facilities constructed to project's resilience standards

comment.narrative: The project has achieved the target by the completion of five public building reconstructions, including Kejati (High prosecutors) Office Building, PIP2B Office Building, Bupati Sigi Office Building, meeting hall in Tondo 2, and meeting hall in Pombewe. In addition, The project also reconstructed one additional public buildings, BNN Office Building.

title.narrative: Non-CSRRP housing provided with water supply system

comment.narrative: The water supply system has been built to serve 8,000 housing units in non-CSRRP housing areas. The water supply system consists of: (i) water treatment plant for Huntap Tondo 1, Tondo 2 & Talise, Kota Palu, that also covers area of Nanumbuku, Wavu, and Kinta, Tadulako University, and housing areas near Tondo; (ii) water treatment plant for Huntap Duyu, that also covers areas of Huntap Duyu, Huntap Balaroa, Kelurahan Duyu and Kelurahan Balaroa; (iii) water treatment plant for Huntap Pombewe that covers area of Huntap Pombewe, Loru village, and Pombewe village; (iv) reservoir (v) distribution piped network in Palu and Sigi; and (vi) housing connections in Palu and Sigi.
